record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some figure text and layout are garbled or flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The study probes intermediate arithmetic states and uses an attention-mask intervention to test whether later computation can rely on information at an earlier position. This is a different method and task from the claim’s rhyme example.
record.gate_note: The paper tests implicit intermediate-state formation and use during iterative arithmetic, not rhyme planning. Ordinary answer-accuracy curves in Figures 1–3 are not rows because they do not measure the proposed hidden-state mechanism or its causal use. The paper’s example instruction to answer “apple” is a task prompt, not an instruction addressed to an AI reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The study probes operator-token hidden states for intermediate sums in iterative addition. At a '+' token the next token is an unpredictable operand, so a decodable running sum there is a feature computed for later use. This bears on V3 (pre-caching) in a new arithmetic setting. It does not test rhyme planning (V1, V4), future-token decoding (V2), or look-ahead toward future outputs (V5). Its loss of state resolution along the sequence is about lossy accumulation, not planning horizon, so it does not bear on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that LLMs form implicit discrete state representations of intermediate results at operator tokens, and that these states lose resolution along the sequence. They also conclude that the attention-bridge experiment shows models use information at intermediate operator tokens, rather than computing from all prior numbers at once, and that the addition proceeds linearly.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic iterative arithmetic, operator-token probes, and an attention-mask bridge intervention; it does not use rhyme-word attribution or rhyme-changing interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: State probe accuracy varies with sequence position and layer group. A prompt telling the model to ignore the formula leaves first-ten-layer probe accuracy unaffected but significantly reduces later-layer accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Digit-wise intermediate states form independently, lowest digit first. Suffix-sum probes indicate linear sequential accumulation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLMs track discrete intermediate arithmetic states in hidden layers without chain-of-thought (latent multi-step state tracking).

record.problems: The authors state that the experiments use only a synthetic mathematical dataset and that task diversity is unsatisfactory. The attention-mask intervention causes a significant accuracy drop; the authors suggest the model is unaccustomed to the abrupt mask change. Several condition-specific intervention values are shown only in a figure.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out. Ordinary iterative-addition accuracy results in Figures 1–3 were omitted because they do not measure hidden-state representation or its causal use.

untested.parts: Tasks other than synthetic iterative arithmetic. No myopic-training or breadcrumbs-vs-pre-caching comparison. No causal intervention on the intermediate-sum state itself.
All parts; no verse or rhyme.
All parts; probes decode arithmetic states, not future tokens.
Look-ahead toward future outputs in reasoning, chess, or Sokoban. Intermediate sums summarize past input, not a planned future.
Planning horizon or incidental-heuristic explanations of plans.

missing.what: Whole-number probe accuracies by operator position for DeepSeek-67B
Digit-wise (3-digit sum) probing by position, showing a sharp decline after the 2nd '+' in later layers
Subtraction probing at the 2nd sign showing early layers compute the formula's value

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Wu et al. (2404.00859) and Future Lens but is not an original source. Pre-caching is inferred: the paper never contrasts pre-caching with side-effect computation. The bridge sits at the first '+', before any sum exists, so it is weak evidence that precomputed sums are used. MLP probes may themselves compute sums from operand information, which weakens decodability as evidence. The record's V5 and V6 links were removed.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyme-word representation before a verse line and interventions that change the line to fit a different rhyme.
Predicting tokens several positions ahead from a single hidden state; the probes decode arithmetic states, not future tokens.
Whether this occurs outside iterative arithmetic; whether the represented features were computed specifically for later positions rather than also arising as a side effect of next-token prediction.
Rhyme planning in smaller open models using open attribution-graph or probing tools.
Chess, Sokoban, other non-arithmetic tasks, and other architectures.
Whether apparent planning in other tasks or models is shallow or incidental; this study measures arithmetic-state resolution and use.

rows.subject: Qwen-72B
rows.operation_detail: Use separate probes to predict individual digits of intermediate sums in 3-digit addition.
rows.measure: Relationship between individual-digit exact accuracies and overall exact accuracy
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: The product of the individual-digit exact accuracies equals the overall exact accuracy.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as evidence that the model establishes independent digit-wise IDSRs.
rows.check: Digit-independence of probe accuracies characterizes the state's format, not whether it is computed for later positions. The text locates this in Section 6.1 (second addition sign), with Fig. 7 covering digit order.

rows.subject: Qwen-72B
rows.operation_detail: Probe hidden states for sums of suffixes and the complete expression in a 2-digit addition task.

conditions.value: all four; last three; last two; last one

rows.measure: Layer-wise probe-accuracy peak order for suffix sums
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: The all-four sum peaks after the last-three sum; the last-two sum peaks several layers earlier.
rows.note: The authors interpret this ordering as evidence for linear, rather than logarithmic, sequential addition.
rows.check: The linear-vs-logarithmic peak order characterizes the computation strategy, not pre-caching or look-ahead.

rows.subject: Qwen-72B
rows.operation_detail: Probe operator-token hidden states under prompts that tell the model to ignore the formula and answer with a word.

conditions.value: negative prompt; example says ignore the formula and answer with apple

rows.measure: Probe accuracy for the numerical addition result
rows.baseline: Baseline prompt; exact value not stated
rows.value: Maximum accuracy in the first ten layers remains unaffected.
rows.note: The reported prompt effect differs by layer group.
rows.check: Early-layer sums persist when the prompt says to ignore the formula. This suggests task-independent, possibly incidental computation. It cannot show the effect V3 names; it is used here as a scope qualifier.

rows.subject: Qwen-72B
rows.operation_detail: Probe operator-token hidden states under prompts that tell the model to ignore the formula and answer with a word.

rows.measure: Probe accuracy for the numerical addition result
rows.baseline: Baseline prompt; exact value not stated

rows.check: Later-layer sum states weaken when the sum is no longer needed for the eventual answer. This is consistent with features being computed for later use.

relationships.condition: Qwen-72B, iterative addition, '+' operator tokens (2nd–3rd), later and early layers
relationships.reason: Running sums are decodable at '+' positions where they cannot aid next-token prediction (R1, R2, R6–R10). Later-layer sum states weaken when a prompt makes the sum irrelevant (R23).
relationships.display_finding: Running sums were decodable where they could not aid next-token prediction, and later-layer sum representations weakened when the prompt made sums irrelevant.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Qwen-72B, iterative addition, '+' operator tokens (2nd–3rd), later and early layers
source_check.reason: Running-sum decodability at '+' positions and task-sensitive later-layer representations support the pre-caching interpretation in this setting. This is indirect evidence; R10 at the final '=' does not independently support V3, and training incentives remain untested.

relationships.condition: Later operator positions; attention-bridge intervention; early layers under an ignore-formula prompt
relationships.reason: Later-layer probe accuracy falls to 74%, 62% and 37% (R3–R5). The bridge mask keeps only non-trivial accuracy with a significant drop, and it routes addend information, not a sum (R11–R19). Early-layer sums form regardless of task (R22).
relationships.display_finding: Later-layer probe accuracy fell to 74%, 62%, and 37%, while bridge masking substantially reduced accuracy but preserved some performance through addend information rather than a computed sum, and early-layer sums formed regardless of task.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Later operator positions; attention-bridge intervention; early layers under an ignore-formula prompt
source_check.reason: Narrow the condition to reduced later-layer resolution at the fourth and fifth '+' (R3–R4). The final '=' concerns next-token-relevant computation; the bridge does not isolate a computed sum; unchanged early-layer probes do not establish the cause of computation. Those conditions cannot independently supply V3 scope-limit verdicts.

relation.reason: The study directly investigates the presence, formation, and possible later use of intermediate arithmetic representations.

tranche.reason: Synthetic iterative arithmetic supplies a new setting with operator-token representations and task-relevance results bearing on V3.

source_check.notes: The supplied source is the named-author v2 revision dated 4 Aug 2026; the pack's anonymous-submission metadata is stale. Probing supports intermediate representations, while the bridge establishes operand-information routing rather than causal use of a decoded sum.

statements.correction: Sections 4.1.3 and 5.3: default probes are one-hidden-layer MLPs; separate single-layer comparisons show layer-dependent linearity and later nonlinear representations. Sections 5.1 and 6.3: running-sum decoding at operator tokens; later-layer decoding decreases under the ignore-formula prompt. Header: arXiv:2407.11421v2, 4 Aug 2026; Junhao Chen, Shengding Hu, Zhiyuan Liu, Maosong Sun.
statements.problem: The reported sum-decoding results are not established as linear-probe results. The supplied text is also a named-author revision, not an anonymous ACL submission. Section 5.1 specifies ten possible sums without explicitly identifying that experiment as one-digit-operand addition.

statements.correction: Section 6.4.1: first '+' bridge; first addend directly masked from subsequent tokens; 2–10 numbers; non-trivial exact-answer accuracy with a significant baseline drop. Computed intermediate-sum use is not isolated.
statements.problem: The experimental description is correct, but its accuracy drop does not itself establish a scope limit on V3: the intervention routes operand information rather than isolating a precomputed sum.

statements.correction: Section 6.3 and Figure 9: maximum first-ten-layer probe accuracies remain unaffected by the ignore-formula prompt; later-layer accuracies significantly decrease. Training incentives and causal dependence on later use are not tested.
statements.problem: Unchanged early-layer probing under one task-changing prompt does not establish that early computation never depends on later use.

statements.correction: Operator-token probes decode intermediate sums. The attention intervention demonstrates a route for first-addend information through the first '+'. No myopic-training, gradient-decomposition, or direct intermediate-sum intervention is reported.
statements.problem: This study does not causally demonstrate later use of the decoded intermediate sum, and it does not explicitly frame its limitation as a test of training rewards.

statements.correction: Section 6.3 and Figure 9: early-layer probe maxima persist under the ignore-formula prompt; later-layer accuracies decrease. The origin of these computations in next-token versus later-position training incentives is not separated.
statements.problem: The prompt result is accurate, but it does not identify early-layer sums specifically as breadcrumbs or establish both causal mechanisms.

statements.correction: Qwen-72B: intermediate sums are decodable at operator tokens; their resolution depends on layer, position, and task prompt. The bridge intervention routes first-addend information. No direct causal intermediate-sum intervention or training-incentive comparison is reported.
statements.problem: For this study, the phrase combining decoded intermediates with causal later use can imply a causal test of the intermediate-sum representation that was not performed. Cross-study counts and authorship comparisons cannot be checked from this text.
